# PR #153 correctness review

## A. Verdict

**block** at `37056e3e0776866578461068ad0d623d6749a6be`.

Two P2 findings: the unresponsive branch bypasses current scope brakes, and the context-size cache can permanently miss an idle seat's new report. **0039-before-0038 migration ordering is supported**, with the conditions below.

## B. Scope

Full PR-owned delta from merge-base `c3895da518aad2047749b87dc9c6663592e357e2`; no wholesale rereview of imported main. The detached worktree remained clean and pinned. No local builds/tests, mutations, live fleet probes or product edits.

#135 remains separate and on hold. F84 billing and independently assigned security/performance assessments are outside this correctness verdict.

## C. Acceptance coverage

| AC | Source/test disposition |
|---|---|
| ac-0001: active scope | Pure scope tests cover current working observations, the 20-minute window, unknown state, usage-limit inactivity and initial worker-count suppression. **F001 bypasses the brakes after a dormant claim exists.** |
| ac-0002: missing PA | Normal 20-minute send, last-holder command, cap and live-PA rearm pass. Restart coverage recreates the watchdog against the persisted store, not a new daemon process. |
| ac-0003: dormant PA | Normal 30-minute wake, working-PA exclusion and turn-based rearm pass. Delivery uses the existing audited wake path; a standing claim prevents repeated admitted wakes. |
| ac-0004: unresponsive PA | Normal 10-minute escalation, receipt and once-per-stretch cap pass. **F001 permits escalation in a currently disallowed scope.** |
| ac-0005: large-seat FYI | Initial crossing, fleet descendants, outsider exclusion, batching and no-wake held FYIs pass. **F002 breaks updates/rearm for cached idle seats.** |
| ac-0006: Copilot size | Extension test captures root usage on the existing activity post; reported-context overlay preserves known transcript facts and session separation. HTTP tests cover state-card propagation and cold-guard parity, including unknown-size admission. **F002 prevents the watchdog from consuming some reports.** |
| ac-0007: restart safety | All four message paths await a stored claim before sending; INSERT OR IGNORE and the composite key suppress duplicate acquisition. Tracker-reset tests retain claims. A crash between claim and send conservatively loses that message; no actual crash-injection test was run. |
| ac-0008: cost | The dedicated single-test binary executes 45 post-warm-up rounds with all four message kinds and unchanged launch counts; a new repository provides a positive launch control. This is fixture/warm-cache proof, not live AFTER cost proof. |
| ac-0009: audit/docs | Thresholds, four messages and changed-verdict audit fields are documented. Tests verify waiting/sent/capped/rearmed audit transitions. DD validation in CI is explicitly unavailable. |

No whole-plan completion is approved; plan/AC/backpressure states remain unchecked.

## D. F001: unresponsive escalation ignores the scope's current brakes

**P2**, `crates/core/src/watchdog.rs:700-729`; caller `crates/daemon/src/pa_presence.rs:509-536,602-644`.

`pa_verdicts` handles an existing dormant claim before checking activity or worker count. Once ten minutes have elapsed, it returns `unresponsive: Send` whenever a prime exists, even with `Activity::Inactive` and only one worker. The caller deliberately continues checking any PA with a dormant claim, so no outer brake prevents the send.

Concrete ordering: an active two-worker fleet causes the dormant wake; a worker then closes, or a usage limit stops the scope; the PA stays silent. Ten minutes after the claim, this branch still wakes the prime. ac-0001 explicitly says a scope below two workers never fires ac-0002 through ac-0004, and a usage-limited scope is inactive.

**Repair:** apply the current activity/minimum-worker brakes to unresponsive emission without resetting the dormant cap. Keep positive PA-turn rearm working even while the scope is inactive. Add post-wake regressions for worker count falling below two and a scope becoming usage-limited. Current tests check those brakes only before a dormant claim exists.

Proof: source/dataflow, not a local reproduction.

## E. F002: cached idle seats never refresh after a new context report

**P2**, `crates/daemon/src/pa_presence.rs:792-829`; report producer `http/fyi.rs:248-255`.

`refresh_sizes` rereads only seats currently working, working at the previous round, or lacking a map entry. An initial unknown/failed read inserts an entry containing `None`, which therefore stops idle retries despite the comment promising retries when no size exists.

A successful cached size also remains forever for an idle seat. A turn can start and finish between 60-second rounds, leaving the seat idle at both snapshots while its activity post reports a new size. The reported-context source is updated, but no cache invalidation or report generation reaches `refresh_sizes`.

For example, after caching 500k for an idle seat, an activity post reports 650k while the seat is idle again. `sizes.contains_key` is true and both working conditions are false: no read, no crossing and no FYI. Conversely, a newly reported compacted size cannot rearm an old large-seat claim. The current crossing test explicitly keeps an idle seat's stale claim while testing rearm only on the working seat.

**Repair:** distinguish an entry with no known size from a successful cached size, and invalidate/recheck cached idle sizes when a new report, completed turn or incarnation change makes them stale. Preserve bounded reads and the unchanged-idle optimization. Add integration cases for an initial unknown idle seat receiving a size, and a reported crossing/compaction between rounds without a working snapshot.

Proof: source/dataflow, not a local reproduction.

## F. Migration ordering

Cargo.lock pins sqlx-core **0.8.6**. Its [Migrator::run_direct](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/blob/v0.8.6/sqlx-core/src/migrate/migrator.rs) builds a map of applied versions and applies each migration absent from that map; it does not compare pending versions only against the maximum applied version. Its [source resolver](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/blob/v0.8.6/sqlx-core/src/migrate/source.rs) sorts versions ascending.

Thus a future binary containing both 0038 and the already-applied 0039 will apply 0038 and skip unchanged 0039. Repository boot (`store/src/migrate.rs:154-207`) always runs that migrator, then resets `user_version` to its compile-time SCHEMA_VERSION, preventing a lower migration's pragma from leaving the cache downgraded.

Conditions: the future binary must retain 0039 and its checksum, and keep SCHEMA_VERSION at least 39. Missing applied migrations, changed checksums or an older binary correctly refuse. This conclusion is pinned-producer and repository source proof, not a local migration replay.

## G. Exact-head CI and commands

[Run 42365178455](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42365178455), attempts **1 and 2**, names this full head and passes all four jobs. Downloaded JUnit contains **2,076 executed cases, zero failures/errors**; the Rust log separately reports five skipped cases.

Named passing cases include activity/window and missing-PA trackers, lone-worker suppression, working-PA exclusion, dormant/escalation/rearm, batched large-seat FYIs, reported-context overlay/card/cold parity and the dedicated launch test. Both Node versions report **2,204 Vitest passed, six skipped**, and **325 combined native-extension passed**. The latest [Delivers run 42365832559](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42365832559) also passed; PR is CLEAN.

Read-only git scope/status, source/spec/test/docs inspection, exact-head CI logs/JUnit and pinned public sqlx source were used. Green CI does not cover either finding's missing transition.

## H. Handover and harness feedback

Return a repaired frozen head with post-wake brake and reported-idle-size regressions, preserving claims-before-send and no added timer/launch. Independent security/performance verdicts and deployment measurements remain owed.

**magicWand:** test transitions after a claim and after a cached observation, not just initial conditions. Those are the two places the normal happy-path tests missed.
